Rule implementation: - src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts - JSDoc: * @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md * @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION * @req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE - Exports an ESLint RuleModule: * meta.type: "problem" * meta.docs.description: "Require @story and @req annotations on code branches" * meta.fixable: "code" * meta.messages.missingAnnotation: "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}." * meta.schema defines an options object with optional branchTypes array. - create(context): * Calls validateBranchTypes(context) from ../utils/branch-annotation-helpers. * If validateBranchTypes returns a listener (invalid config), returns it directly. * Otherwise treats result as branchTypes array and builds handlers for each branch type. * For each branch type, registers a handler that: - Skips default SwitchCase nodes (node.test == null). - Calls reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef).
Branch helper utilities: - src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts - DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES (annotated with @story 004.0 and @req REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA): ["IfStatement", "SwitchCase", "TryStatement", "CatchClause", "ForStatement", "ForOfStatement", "ForInStatement", "WhileStatement", "DoWhileStatement"]. -> Satisfies REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION and REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA. - validateBranchTypes(context) (annotated with REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE): * Reads context.options[0] || {}. * If options.branchTypes is an array: - Filters out invalid types using DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES.includes. - If invalidTypes.length > 0, returns { Program: ProgramHandler } where ProgramHandler: + Calls context.report for each invalid type t with message: `Value "${t}" should be equal to one of the allowed values: ${DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES.join(", ")}`. -> Implements the invalid configuration error behavior described in the story. - Otherwise returns the provided branchTypes as BranchType[]. * If no branchTypes provided, returns Array.from(DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES). -> Satisfies REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION (simple, per-node logic). - gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node) (annotated with REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION): * For SwitchCase: - Uses sourceCode.lines and node.loc.start.line. - Scans up to PRE_COMMENT_OFFSET (= 2) lines above the case line. - While lines match /^\s*(\/\/|\/\*)/, collects them into an array and joins with spaces. -> Associates nearby line/block comments with a SwitchCase, handling blank-line edge cases. * For other nodes: - Uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node) to get leading comments. - Maps comment nodes to c.value and joins with spaces. -> Satisfies REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION and supports nested structures because it operates per node. - reportMissingStory(context, node, { indent, insertPos, storyFixCountRef }) (annotated with REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING): * If storyFixCountRef.count === 0: - context.report with messageId "missingAnnotation", data { missing: "@story" } and a fixer that inserts: `${indent}// @story .story.md\n` at [insertPos, insertPos]. - Increments storyFixCountRef.count. * Else: - context.report without fixer for missing "@story". - reportMissingReq(context, node, { indent, insertPos, missingStory }) (annotated with REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING): * If !missingStory: - context.report with messageId "missingAnnotation", data { missing: "@req" } and fixer inserting: `${indent}// @req \n`. * Else: - context.report without fixer for missing "@req". - reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef) (annotated with REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING): * Gets sourceCode via context.getSourceCode(). * text = gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node). * missingStory = !/@story\b/.test(text); missingReq = !/@req\b/.test(text). * Computes indent from leading whitespace on the branch's start line. * insertPos from sourceCode.getIndexFromLoc({ line: node.loc.start.line, column: 0 }). * Builds actions array with entries for story and req and forEach over it, invoking reportMissingStory/reportMissingReq when missing. -> Satisfies REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING and supports nested branches by design.
Tests for rule behavior and configuration: - tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts - Header: * @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md * @story docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md * @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION and multiple error-reporting requirements. - Uses ESLint RuleTester with ecmaVersion 2020 and the require-branch-annotation rule. - Valid cases exercise multiple branch kinds and comment styles (REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION): * Switch with case 'z' preceded by line comments containing @story and @req. * IfStatement with preceding line comments for @story and @req. * For loop with block comments for @story and @req. * Switch with annotated case and default. * Try/finally annotated with block comments. * Try with annotated catch. * Do-while, for-of, for-in, while loops each annotated with block comments. * Switch-case with inline annotation right above the case. * Default switch case without annotations is valid (default branch is exempt via node.test == null handling). * Custom branchTypes: ["IfStatement"] ensures switch is ignored; ["IfStatement", "SwitchCase"] enforces both. - Invalid cases verify detection, autofix, and error messages (Core Functionality, User Experience, Error Handling): * Missing annotations on if-statement: - code: `if (condition) {}` - output adds `// @story .story.md` above, and expects two errors with data missing: "@story" and "@req". * For loop with only @story: - output adds `// @req `; error for missing "@req". * While loop with only @req: - output inserts `// @story .story.md` above; error for missing "@story". * Switch-case without comments: - output inserts `// @story .story.md` before the case; errors for missing "@story" and "@req". * Do-while, for-of, for-in, try-catch: each produce expected numbers of missingAnnotation errors and appropriate autofixes where defined. * Switch-case with a blank line before case: - output shows annotation inserted above the case, testing SwitchCase scanning edge case. * Custom branchTypes for ForStatement: enforces ForStatement only and produces missingAnnotation errors with autofix output. - Second RuleTester.run block: * Invalid configuration test with options: [{ branchTypes: ["UnknownType"] }]. * Expects an error whose message matches /should be equal to one of the allowed values/. -> Confirms invalid configuration behavior per REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE.

traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS are satisfied based on concrete implementation and tests: - Core Functionality: The require-branch-annotation rule and its helpers detect missing @story and @req annotations across all configured significant branch types (if/else, try/catch, switch cases, loops) and support autofix for missing annotations where appropriate. - Quality Standards: The rule is implemented as a proper ESLint RuleModule with meta.type, meta.docs, schema, and messages, and is tested via ESLint RuleTester plus dedicated helper unit tests, following ESLint best practices. The logic is straightforward and efficient, suitable for large files. - Integration: The rule is wired into the plugin’s dynamic rule loading (RULE_NAMES and rules map), included in the recommended/strict flat configs, and listed in README; tests cover various patterns and branch types, and nested structures are inherently supported because the rule operates per branch node. - User Experience: Error messages clearly specify which annotation is missing (using messageId "missingAnnotation" and {{missing}} placeholder). Autofix behavior provides helpful placeholder annotations. Invalid configuration is reported with explicit messages listing allowed branch types. - Error Handling: Invalid branchTypes configurations return a safe Program listener that reports configuration errors without crashing ESLint. Edge cases like default switch cases and comments separated by blank lines are handled explicitly in code and tests. - Documentation: docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md and README.md provide rule description, configuration options, valid/invalid examples, and invalid configuration behavior, all aligned with the story’s requirements. Tests are present and (per npm test run) execute without reported failures. Therefore this story is fully implemented and passes.
